questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several factors influenced my choice of study destination. First and foremost, the quality of education and the reputation of the institution played a significant role. I wanted to study at a university known for its strong academic programs and research opportunities in my field of interest. Beyond academics, factors such as living costs, student life, and cultural experiences also mattered. I was looking for a place that offered a good balance between affordability and quality of life. Lastly, career opportunities and networking possibilities in the country after graduation were crucial in my decision-making process.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would rate my overall study abroad experience very highly. It has been an incredibly enriching journey, both academically and personally. Studying in a new environment allowed me to gain a global perspective, improve my adaptability, and connect with people from diverse backgrounds. The quality of education, student support services, and extracurricular opportunities exceeded my expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Finding the necessary information upon arrival was somewhat challenging. While the university provided some resources, such as orientation sessions and online guides, not everything was clearly explained. Some important details, like setting up a bank account, understanding healthcare options, and local transportation, required a lot of independent research.

I often had to ask other students or university staff for help, which sometimes took time. A more structured and detailed guide for international students would have made the process much easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
When I arrived at my study destination, I received helpful assistance. The university provided an orientation program that covered important information about academics, student services, and daily life. There were also support staff and student mentors available to answer questions, which made things easier.

Some practical matters, like setting up a bank account and understanding public transportation, still required some effort, but overall, the information was accessible, and I was able to find help when needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall, I was quite satisfied with the orientation and assistance provided by my host institution upon arrival. The orientation program was well-organized and covered essential topics like academics, student services, and campus facilities. The support staff and student mentors were also helpful in answering questions and providing guidance.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding off-campus housing was quite difficult for me. The process was more complicated than I initially expected. There were limited listings available, and many of them were either too expensive or already taken. I spent a lot of time searching online, reaching out to landlords, and checking notice boards around campus.
My recommendation would be to start looking as early as possible and to be proactive in contacting landlords. It can also be helpful to network with other students, as they may know of available places or have advice on where to look. If possible, visiting the area in person before committing to a place would be a good idea.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Future exchange students should know that living off-campus can be both rewarding and challenging. It offers more independence, but it also requires a bit more planning. One of the main things to keep in mind is that off-campus housing can be more expensive and harder to find, so it's essential to start searching early.

Additionally, you'll need to consider transportation options to get to campus, as commuting can be time-consuming, especially if you're living far from the university. Utilities like internet, water, and electricity are usually not included in rent, so be prepared for extra costs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process of finding a place to live took longer than I expected, and there were some unexpected costs involved. However, once I settled in, I appreciated the independence and the opportunity to experience life outside the campus. In the end, it worked out, but I would recommend future students start their housing search early and be prepared for the possibility of higher living costs.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the registration process at my host institution to be somewhat difficult. While the university provided online portals and guidelines, there were a few steps that were unclear, especially as an international student.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at my host institution was difficult and very time-consuming. There were many steps involved, and the system was not always straightforward. I had to navigate through various online portals, fill out numerous forms, and wait for confirmations, which often took longer than expected.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The help available during the registration process was limited. There was only one online meeting offered to assist students, which provided some basic information, but it didn’t cover all the details or specific challenges I faced. While the meeting was helpful in some respects, I still had to figure out many things on my own and contact various departments for further assistance. More accessible and ongoing support would have been beneficial, as it would have made the process smoother.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I wasn’t entirely successful in registering for the classes I wanted. Due to limited spots or conflicting schedules, I wasn’t able to secure a place in some of the courses I had hoped for. I had to adjust my schedule and choose alternative classes, which was frustrating at times.

While I was eventually able to register for enough courses to meet my academic requirements, the process felt a bit stressful and competitive. I would recommend future students to be flexible with their choices and register as early as possible to avoid missing out on preferred courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice to future exchange students regarding registration at my host institution would be to book a meeting with the study advisor as early as possible. The registration process can be complicated, and having a study advisor guide you through the steps will save you time and help avoid potential issues. They can offer valuable advice on course selection, prerequisites, and scheduling conflicts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of courses at my host institution was similar to those at my home university. The academic rigor and expectations were comparable, with courses covering a similar depth of material. The professors focused on delivering content that challenged students while still being accessible and engaging.

However, I did notice some differences in the teaching style and the way assignments were structured. The format of assessments and the level of interaction in class varied slightly, but overall, I felt well-prepared to handle the coursework. The course workload was manageable, and I didn’t experience any major difficulties adjusting to the academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching at my host institution was quite similar to that of UCPH. Both universities emphasized a combination of lectures, group work, and independent study. Professors at both institutions encouraged student participation and critical thinking, and there was a focus on understanding the material rather than just memorizing it.

The main difference I noticed was in the level of interaction and the use of digital platforms. At my host institution, there was a greater reliance on online tools and resources for course materials and communication, which made it easier to access information. However, overall, the teaching style, academic expectations, and approach to learning were very similar to my experience at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend the course EM1517 Reporting and Sustainability Accounting (6.0 ECTS) to future exchange students. The reason for this recommendation is largely due to the professor, who made the course engaging and insightful. The professor’s teaching style was very clear, and they provided valuable real-world examples, which helped in understanding complex topics. The course content is also highly relevant, particularly for those interested in sustainability and corporate reporting, making it a great choice for anyone looking to expand their knowledge in this area.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: One unexpected cost I encountered was a higher deposit for my accommodation than I had anticipated. The deposit was significantly more than I expected, which put extra pressure on my budget at the time. It wasn't clearly mentioned in the housing agreement, so it was a bit of a surprise. Aside from that, other smaller costs, such as course materials or administrative fees, also added up, but the deposit was the biggest unexpected expense.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was actually less expensive than I had expected. I was pleasantly surprised by how affordable grocery shopping and eating out were, especially compared to what I was used to at home. Many local markets offered fresh produce at reasonable prices, and there were also affordable meal options available near campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was somewhat disappointed with the non-academic opportunities at my host institution. While there were several clubs and sports activities available, there were no badminton options, which was something I was really hoping to participate in. This made it harder for me to stay active in the way I was used to.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
At my host institution, there were several cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students. The university offered a variety of clubs, including cultural exchange groups, language clubs, and social meet-ups, which allowed students to connect and share their backgrounds. There were also some events celebrating local festivals and traditions, providing great opportunities to experience the local culture.

In terms of athletics, the university had access to general fitness facilities, as well as sports teams for common sports like football, basketball, and volleyball. Unfortunately, there were no badminton options, which was a bit disappointing for me.

Socially, there were regular student events, like themed parties, movie nights, and pub nights, where students could meet and socialize. Overall, the campus offered a vibrant social scene, but I would have appreciated a wider range of athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend participating in picnic events to future exchange students. These are a great way to relax, enjoy the outdoors, and meet people from different backgrounds in a casual setting. The picnics often take place in beautiful parks or on campus lawns, creating a laid-back atmosphere perfect for making new friends and experiencing local culture. It’s also an affordable and fun way to spend time with fellow students outside of class.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend visiting the Dolomites during weekends or holidays. The stunning mountain range offers incredible opportunities for hiking, skiing, or simply enjoying the breathtaking views. Whether you’re into outdoor adventures or just want to relax and take in the scenery, the Dolomites provide a perfect escape from the city. It’s an unforgettable experience that gives you the chance to connect with nature and explore some of the most beautiful landscapes in the region.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust to the local culture of my exchange site. The people were welcoming, and there was a strong sense of community, which made it easy to settle in. I enjoyed exploring the local traditions, food, and customs, and was able to connect with both locals and other international students. While there were a few cultural differences, they were mostly interesting to experience, and I quickly adapted to the new environment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
One cultural difference I found particularly challenging was the pace of life. In my host country, people tend to take their time with daily activities, which was a bit slower than I was used to. This meant I had to adjust to a more relaxed approach to time, whether it was during meals or social events.

Another challenge was the language barrier. While many people spoke English, there were still situations where local language skills were important, especially in more informal settings. It took some time to feel comfortable navigating conversations outside of academic or tourist environments.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I most appreciated about the local culture was the relaxing and laid-back style of life. People seemed to really value taking time to enjoy simple moments, whether it was savoring a meal, spending time with friends, or just enjoying the outdoors. This slower pace helped me to feel less stressed and more present, and it gave me the chance to appreciate the little things in life. It was a refreshing change and something I’ve come to value during my time abroad.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
he three most important things I would tell a UCPH student going to my host institution on exchange are:

Check the course offerings carefully: Make sure to look through the courses available and confirm that they align with your academic interests and requirements. Some courses may have prerequisites or specific registration dates, so it’s important to plan ahead.

Double-check the exam dates: Exam schedules can sometimes differ from what you might expect, so it’s essential to verify the exam dates early on. This will help you avoid any surprises and ensure you’re prepared.

Complete the Online Learning Agreement (OLA): Don’t forget to make sure your OLA is completed and approved. This is a crucial step in ensuring that your credits transfer smoothly back to UCPH, and it helps avoid any administrative issues later on.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
One thing I would recommend is to get familiar with the local transportation system early on. While most places are accessible by public transport, knowing the best routes, passes, and how to navigate the system can save you time and money.

Additionally, take advantage of any international student networks or meetups. These groups can help you adjust to life at the host institution and offer advice on everything from housing to local customs.

Lastly, be open to exploring local traditions and events – there are often festivals, markets, or community activities that provide great opportunities to immerse yourself in the culture and meet new people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: he most rewarding part of my exchange experience was definitely meeting new people. I had the chance to connect with students from all over the world, learn about different cultures, and form lasting friendships. These interactions not only made my time abroad more enjoyable but also broadened my perspective and enriched my personal growth. It was inspiring to hear others' stories, share experiences, and build a sense of community with people from diverse backgrounds.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was that the subjects I took did not overlap. This made it more difficult to ensure that the courses I completed abroad would count towards my degree requirements. It required extra effort to plan my course selection carefully and make sure that I could meet all necessary academic goals. While it worked out in the end, the lack of alignment between the two institutions added some complexity to my exchange experience.

questions.answer: Yes
